country.name: Slovenia
country.tagline: A small country with three wine worlds: Collio's mirror in Brda, the bora-swept Karst, and the steep Styrian hills where the world's oldest vine still fruits.

stats.note: Vineyard area: Eurostat apro_cpsh1, 13.9 kha in 2025 (the ministry cites about 17,000 ha cultivated and 14,600 ha registered). Production: OIV figure of 512,800 hl for 2024.

country.overview:
Slovenia packs Alpine, Mediterranean, Pannonian and Dinaric landscapes into a country smaller than New Jersey, and its wine follows those seams. There are three regions. Primorska in the west runs from the Italian border at Goriška Brda through the Vipava valley and the limestone Karst to the Istrian coast at Koper; it is a continuation of Friuli's Collio and Carso, with Rebula (Ribolla Gialla), Malvazija, Refošk and the local Zelen and Pinela. Podravje in the north-east, the Drava basin, is Styrian and Pannonian country of steep, terraced hills (Štajerska Slovenija, plus Prekmurje beyond the Mura) making crisp, aromatic whites: Laški rizling, Šipon (Furmint), Sauvignon Blanc, Renski rizling, Traminec and Ranina. Posavje in the south-east, along the Sava and Krka, is the land of light, tart blends: Cviček, Metliška črnina, Bizeljčan.

Vineyards cover roughly 14,000 to 17,000 ha depending on who is counting, worked by more than 27,000 holdings averaging just over half a hectare. Production runs around 0.5 million hl; about three-quarters is white, most is drunk at home, and up to 70% carries a geographical designation. The structure is very small-scale: thousands of weekend vineyards (*zidanice*, small vineyard cottages, dot the hills) next to a few large cooperatives such as Klet Brda, Vinakoper, Ptujska klet and Radgonske gorice.

Why does a country this small matter to a wine nerd? Partly because it sits on so many borders. Brda is the same hill system as Italy's Collio, cut by a frontier drawn in 1947 that left families with vines on both sides; the Karst runs straight into Italy's Carso; Štajerska is the southern half of historical Styria, whose northern half is Austria's Südsteiermark; Prekmurje looks across to Hungary. Comparing wines across those lines is one of the best lessons in terroir versus culture that Europe offers.

Slovenia's outsized fame comes from the west. Along the Italian border, growers such as Movia, Klinec, Batič, Kabaj, Čotar and Mlečnik, alongside their friends across the border in Oslavia, revived long skin-contact fermentation of white grapes in the 1990s and 2000s, and the Brda-Collio-Vipava axis became the heartland of modern 'orange wine'. In the east, the Styrian hills around Jeruzalem, Ormož and Haloze make some of Europe's most precise, high-acid whites and fine sweet wines (*ledeno vino*, ice wine, and *suhi jagodni izbor*, the Trockenbeerenauslese equivalent). Maribor has the world's oldest productive vine, more than 400 years old, and Ptuj has the country's oldest cellar and oldest bottled wine.

history.title: Celts and Illyrians
history.text: The ministry and most histories date local winemaking to Celtic and Illyrian tribes, well before the Romans.

history.title: Roman Poetovio
history.text: Roman Poetovio (Ptuj) on the Drava and the colonies of Istria and the Vipava valley spread viticulture; Ptuj was a major legionary town and trading hub.

history.title: The Minorite cellar of Ptuj
history.text: Ptujska klet traces its symbolic beginning to 1239, when the Minorite friars built a monastery in the centre of Ptuj with a wine cellar beneath it.

history.title: The Old Vine of Maribor
history.text: A Žametovka vine planted on the south wall of a house in Maribor's Lent quarter survived Ottoman raids, phylloxera and war; it is now more than 400 years old and listed by Guinness as the oldest vine in the world.

history.title: Slovenian sparkling wine
history.text: Clotar Bouvier began traditional-method sparkling wine at Gornja Radgona in 1852, the start of what became Radgonske gorice's Zlata Radgonska penina. The Bouvier grape (Ranina) carries his name.

history.title: Phylloxera
history.text: Phylloxera ravaged the Habsburg-ruled Slovenian lands; replanting on American rootstocks favoured international varieties, with local grapes such as Žametovka and Rebula surviving in blends.

history.title: Independence and the EU
history.text: Slovenia was the first Yugoslav republic to leave the federation (1991) and joined the EU in 2004. Cooperatives were restructured and family estates grew quickly.

history.title: The orange wine revival
history.text: Growers on both sides of the Brda-Collio border, from Movia and Batič to Gravner and Radikon in Italy, returned to long skin maceration of white grapes, making Slovenia a reference point for 'orange' or macerated white wine.

country.classification: Slovenia's quality categories (ZGP, *vino z zaščitenim geografskim poreklom*: PDO wine) are tied to its nine wine districts, each a PDO: Goriška Brda, Vipavska dolina, Kras and Slovenska Istra in Primorska; Štajerska Slovenija and Prekmurje in Podravje; Bizeljsko Sremič, Dolenjska and Bela krajina in Posavje. Within PDO wine a label may say *kakovostno vino ZGP* (quality wine) or *vrhunsko vino ZGP* (premium wine, tasting-scored and stricter), and the Prädikat-style terms *pozna trgatev* (late harvest), *izbor*, *jagodni izbor*, *suhi jagodni izbor* and *ledeno vino* apply to sweet wines. Five wines have special status as PTP (*priznano tradicionalno poimenovanje*, recognised traditional designation), each also an EU PDO: Teran (Refošk from the Karst), Cviček (Dolenjska), Metliška črnina and Belokranjec (Bela krajina) and Bizeljčan (Bizeljsko Sremič). A new Wine Act was adopted as a government bill in November 2025 and was in parliament during 2026.
country.climate_soils: Primorska is sub-Mediterranean: warm summers, mild winters and the cold bora wind that sweeps down the Vipava valley. Its soils are flysch (*opoka*, layered marl and sandstone) in Brda and Vipava and red *terra rossa* over limestone on the Karst. Podravje and Posavje are continental and cooler, with steep marl, sandstone and clay hills; Haloze and Jeruzalem have some of the steepest terraces in Central Europe, and Bizeljsko has quartz sands soft enough to dig storage caves (*repnice*).

grapes.name: Rebula
grapes.note: Ribolla Gialla: the signature white of Goriška Brda, both fresh and long-macerated.

grapes.name: Laški rizling
grapes.note: Welschriesling, the most planted grape, from fresh Styrian whites to botrytised sweet wines.

grapes.name: Šipon
grapes.note: The Styrian name for Furmint, high-acid and long-lived around Jeruzalem and Ormož.

grapes.name: Refošk
grapes.note: Refosco dal Peduncolo Rosso: becomes Teran on the Karst's terra rossa and makes a fruity red in Istria.

grapes.name: Malvazija
grapes.note: Istrian Malvasia, the coastal white of Slovenska Istra and Brda.

grapes.name: Zelen and Pinela
grapes.note: Vipava natives: Zelen is herbal and green-fruited, Pinela delicate and nervy.

grapes.name: Vitovska
grapes.note: Karst white grown on terra rossa, often macerated.

grapes.name: Žametovka
grapes.note: Old red variety, the grape of Maribor's Old Vine and a base of Cviček.

grapes.name: Modra frankinja
grapes.note: Blaufränkisch, the main red of Posavje.

grapes.name: Ranina
grapes.note: Bouvier, named for Radgona and Clotar Bouvier.

regions.name: Primorska
regions.tagline: Collio's other half, the bora-blasted Vipava valley, the red earth of the Karst and the Istrian coast.
regions.summary: Primorska ('Littoral') is Slovenia's western wine region, about 6,300 ha across four PDO districts: Goriška Brda (about 1,800 ha), Vipavska dolina (about 2,100 ha), Kras (about 560 ha) and Slovenska Istra (about 1,850 ha). Brda is the eastern half of Friuli's Collio, cut off by the 1947 border, a landscape of flysch hills and hilltop villages making Rebula, Friulano (Sauvignonasse, called Zeleni sauvignon or Jakot locally), Malvazija and Merlot. Vipava is a long valley where the bora wind can gust above 150 km/h; its native Zelen and Pinela grow beside Rebula and international varieties. The Karst is a limestone plateau of red earth, dry stone walls and thin soil famous for Teran and Vitovska. Slovenska Istra, around Koper, Izola and Piran, makes Malvazija and Refošk on the warm coast.
regions.history: Brda and Vipava were Habsburg lands with Venetian influence; Brda was split between Italy and Yugoslavia in 1947, and Klet Brda, founded in 1957 at Dobrovo, gathered the Slovenian side's growers into Slovenia's largest cooperative. The region was the centre of the macerated-white revival from the 1990s.
regions.terroir: Flysch (*opoka*), layered marl and sandstone that crumbles into well-drained soil, in Brda, Vipava and Istra; terra rossa over karst limestone on the Kras. Sub-Mediterranean climate; the bora dries the vines and limits disease.
regions.grapes: Rebula, Malvazija, Zeleni sauvignon, Sauvignon Blanc, Chardonnay, Sivi pinot, Zelen, Pinela, Vitovska; Refošk/Teran, Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon.
regions.styles: Fresh and macerated whites, Teran, Merlot-based reds, sweet Pikolit, traditional-method sparkling (Movia Puro).
regions.classification: Four district PDOs plus the Teran PTP/PDO on the Karst.

regions.name: Podravje
regions.tagline: Steep Styrian terraces and Pannonian plains: crisp aromatic whites, Šipon and the world's oldest vine.
regions.summary: Podravje, the Drava basin in north-east Slovenia, is the largest region and has two PDO districts: Štajerska Slovenija (about 5,400 ha, Slovenian Styria) and Prekmurje (about 440 ha, across the Mura). Štajerska's sub-districts include Maribor, Radgona-Kapela, Ljutomer-Ormož (with the hilltop village of Jeruzalem), Haloze, Slovenske gorice, Šmarje-Virštanj and the Srednje Slovenske gorice. The style is cool-climate whites with piercing acidity: Laški rizling, Šipon, Sauvignon Blanc, Renski rizling, Traminec, Muškat and Kerner, plus sweet late-harvest and ice wines.
regions.history: Roman Poetovio (Ptuj) was a wine town; the Minorites built a cellar there in 1239. Maribor's Old Vine dates to before the mid-17th century. Clotar Bouvier made sparkling wine at Gornja Radgona from 1852. Large socialist-era cellars (Vinag in Maribor, Ptujska klet, Radgonske gorice) still exist.
regions.terroir: Marl, sandstone and clay hills, often terraced on slopes of 30 degrees or more; continental climate with cold winters and warm, dry autumns that allow botrytis and ice wine.
regions.grapes: Laški rizling, Šipon, Sauvignon Blanc, Renski rizling, Sivi pinot, Traminec, Muškat ottonel, Rumeni muškat, Ranina, Kerner, Modra frankinja, Modri pinot.
regions.styles: Dry aromatic whites, late harvest, berry selection and ice wine, traditional-method sparkling.
regions.classification: Two PDO districts; sub-districts appear on labels.

regions.name: Posavje
regions.tagline: The Sava and Krka hills of zidanice cottages, tart Cviček and the sand caves of Bizeljsko.
regions.summary: Posavje, along the Sava and Krka rivers in south-east Slovenia, has three PDO districts: Dolenjska (about 1,350 ha), Bizeljsko Sremič (about 700 ha) and Bela krajina (about 300 ha). It is the country's most traditional wine landscape, with hills covered in small vineyards and weekend cottages (*zidanice*), and its emblem wines are blends rather than varietals: Cviček (light, tart, low-alcohol, made from red and white grapes together), Metliška črnina and Belokranjec in Bela krajina, and Bizeljčan. Fine sweet wines (*ledeno vino*, *jagodni izbor*) and sparkling wines are made in Bizeljsko and Bela krajina too.
regions.history: Monasteries such as Pleterje and Kostanjevica shaped the vineyards in the Middle Ages; a strong smallholder culture survived the socialist period.
regions.terroir: Marl, clay and sandstone hills; Bizeljsko's quartz sands; continental climate.
regions.grapes: Žametovka, Modra frankinja, Kraljevina, Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec, Ranfol, Portugalka, Šentlovrenka, Rumeni muškat.
regions.styles: Light red-white blends (Cviček), red blends (Metliška črnina, Bizeljčan), white blends (Belokranjec), sweet wines and sparkling.
regions.classification: Three district PDOs plus four PTP wines: Cviček, Metliška črnina, Belokranjec and Bizeljčan.

si-bela-krajina.name: Bela krajina
si-bela-krajina.grapes: Modra frankinja, Žametovka, Laški rizling, Kraljevina, Rumeni muškat
si-bela-krajina.summary: Bela krajina ('White March'), named for its birch trees and white linen dress, is a small district (about 300 ha) on the Kolpa river by the Croatian border around Metlika, Semič and Črnomelj. It makes Metliška črnina, Belokranjec, Modra frankinja and some of Slovenia's best ice wines and botrytised sweet wines.

si-belokranjec.name: Belokranjec
si-belokranjec.grapes: Laški rizling, Kraljevina, Beli pinot, Chardonnay, Rumeni muškat, Zeleni silvanec, Renski rizling
si-belokranjec.summary: Belokranjec is the white partner of Metliška črnina: a fresh, fragrant white blend from Bela krajina based on Laški rizling, Kraljevina, Beli pinot, Rumeni muškat and Zeleni silvanec. Its amended specification was approved in March 2026.

si-bizeljcan.name: Bizeljčan
si-bizeljcan.grapes: White: Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec, Ranfol; red: Modra frankinja, Žametovka, Portugalka
si-bizeljcan.summary: Bizeljčan is the recognised traditional designation of Bizeljsko Sremič, made as a white blend (Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec, Ranfol, Kraljevina and others) and as a red (Modra frankinja, Žametovka, Portugalka). Both are light, fresh, everyday wines.

si-bizeljsko-sremic.name: Bizeljsko Sremič
si-bizeljsko-sremic.grapes: Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec, Ranfol, Kraljevina, Modra frankinja, Žametovka
si-bizeljsko-sremic.summary: Bizeljsko Sremič lies in the far east of Posavje by the Croatian border, about 700 ha. Quartz sand under the vineyards let growers dig *repnice*, caves originally for storing turnips (*repa*) that now age wine at a steady temperature. The district makes Bizeljčan blends, sweet wines and traditional-method sparkling (Istenič is the best-known house).

si-cvicek.name: Cviček
si-cvicek.grapes: Žametovka, Modra frankinja, Kraljevina, Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec
si-cvicek.summary: Cviček is a recognised traditional designation for a light, pale red wine from Dolenjska made by blending red and white grapes: mainly Žametovka and Modra frankinja with Kraljevina, Laški rizling and others. It is low in alcohol (typically 8.5 to 10%) and high in acidity, drunk young and cool. Slovenia's ministry approved an amended specification for Cviček in September 2025.
si-cvicek.nerd_note: Cviček is one of the few protected wines in the EU that must blend red and white grapes; its low alcohol made it a 'doctor's wine' recommended to convalescents.

si-dolenjska.name: Dolenjska
si-dolenjska.grapes: Žametovka, Modra frankinja, Kraljevina, Laški rizling, Rumeni plavec
si-dolenjska.summary: Dolenjska is the hilly heart of Posavje around Novo mesto and Trebnje, about 1,350 ha of small vineyards and *zidanice* cottages. It is best known for Cviček but also makes varietal Modra frankinja, Žametovka and whites from Kraljevina, Laški rizling and Rumeni plavec.

si-goriska-brda.name: Goriška Brda
si-goriska-brda.grapes: Rebula, Zeleni sauvignon (Friulano), Malvazija, Chardonnay, Sivi pinot, Sauvignon, Pikolit; Merlot, Cabernet, Pokalca
si-goriska-brda.summary: Goriška Brda ('Gorizia hills') is the Slovenian half of the Collio, a maze of flysch ridges and hilltop villages between the Soča and Idrija rivers on the Italian border, about 1,800 ha. Its signature grape is Rebula (Ribolla Gialla), which makes everything from crisp, citrusy whites to amber wines macerated for months on the skins. Zeleni sauvignon (Friulano), Malvazija, Chardonnay, Sivi pinot and the sweet Pikolit add range; Merlot and Cabernet thrive on the warmer slopes, and the local red Pokalca (Schioppettino) persists. The cooperative Klet Brda in Dobrovo is Slovenia's largest producer, but the district's name abroad comes from family estates: Movia, Klinec, Kabaj, Edi Simčič, Marjan Simčič, Ščurek, Erzetič, Dolfo, Štekar and Gašper.
si-goriska-brda.terroir: Eocene flysch (*opoka*): alternating marl and sandstone that weathers into well-drained, lime-rich soil; terraced slopes of 75 to 400 m; the Julian Alps block cold northern air and the Adriatic is 25 km away.
si-goriska-brda.nerd_note: Movia's Puro sparkling wine is sold undisgorged; the drinker opens it upside down under water (or into a bowl) to release the lees, a theatrical ritual devised by Aleš Kristančič.

si-kras.name: Kras
si-kras.summary: The Kras (Karst) is the limestone plateau behind Trieste, about 560 ha of vineyard in pockets of red earth between dolines, dry-stone walls and sumac. It is the home of Teran, the deep purple, high-acid wine of Refošk grown on terra rossa, and of Vitovska and Malvazija whites, often macerated. Families such as Čotar, Renčel, Lisjak and Štoka in villages like Tomaj, Dutovlje and Gorjansko age their wines in caves cut into the limestone.
si-kras.terroir: Iron-rich terra rossa in hollows of karst limestone, 200 to 400 m; thin soils, drought stress and the bora.
si-kras.nerd_note: Kras growers often have to break the limestone with machines and import soil to plant a vineyard, which is why the district stays tiny.

si-metliska-crnina.name: Metliška črnina
si-metliska-crnina.grapes: Modra frankinja, Žametovka, Portugalka, Šentlovrenka, Gamay, Modri pinot, Zweigelt
si-metliska-crnina.summary: Metliška črnina ('black of Metlika') is Bela krajina's traditional red blend, dominated by Modra frankinja and Žametovka with Portugalka, Šentlovrenka, Gamay and others. It is deep coloured, dry, medium-bodied and fruity. The ministry approved an amended specification in March 2026.

si-prekmurje.name: Prekmurje
si-prekmurje.grapes: Laški rizling, Šipon, Sauvignon, Renski rizling, Beli pinot
si-prekmurje.summary: Prekmurje is the flat-to-rolling Pannonian corner of Slovenia beyond the Mura, bordering Hungary and Austria, with about 440 ha in two hill groups: the Goričko hills and the Lendavske gorice. The wines are Laški rizling, Šipon, Sauvignon and Renski rizling, and the area has a strong Hungarian minority; Marof's Mačkovci winery has given the district international attention.

si-slovenska-istra.name: Slovenska Istra
si-slovenska-istra.grapes: Malvazija, Refošk, Rumeni muškat, Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot
si-slovenska-istra.summary: Slovenska Istra covers the warm flysch hills behind the Slovenian coast at Koper, Izola and Piran, about 1,850 ha. Malvazija is the white and Refošk the red, along with Cabernet, Merlot and the local Muškat. The large Vinakoper cooperative and family wineries such as Santomas, Rojac, Korenika & Moškon and Pucer z Vrha make most of the wine.

si-stajerska-slovenija.name: Štajerska Slovenija
si-stajerska-slovenija.grapes: Laški rizling, Šipon, Sauvignon, Renski rizling, Sivi pinot, Traminec, Muškat, Kerner, Ranina
si-stajerska-slovenija.summary: Štajerska Slovenija is the largest Slovenian district, about 5,400 ha across the steep hills of Slovenian Styria from Maribor and Ptuj to Ljutomer-Ormož, Haloze and Slovenske gorice. It shares its style with Austria's Südsteiermark across the border: racy, aromatic whites from Sauvignon Blanc, Laški rizling, Šipon (Furmint), Renski rizling, Sivi pinot, Traminec, Muškat and Kerner, often grown on terraces at 30 degrees or more, plus late-harvest, botrytis and ice wines. Jeruzalem in Ljutomer-Ormož and the Haloze hills near Ptuj are the classic sites; producers include Puklavec, Verus, Steyer, Gaube, Kogl, Valdhuber, Heaps Good Wine and the old cooperatives Ptujska klet and Vinag.
si-stajerska-slovenija.terroir: Marl, sandstone and clay on steep terraced hills; continental climate with long, cool autumns.
si-stajerska-slovenija.nerd_note: Dveri-Pax is the wine estate of Admont Abbey in Austria, whose Benedictines held vineyards near Jarenina from the 12th century.

si-teran.name: Teran
si-teran.summary: Teran is a recognised traditional designation (PTP) and EU PDO for red wine made 100% from Refošk on the terra rossa of the Kras. The iron-rich soil gives a deep purple wine with very high acidity, sour cherry and blackberry fruit and a reputation in local folk medicine for being good for the blood. Traditionally it is drunk young with Karst prosciutto (*pršut*). Croatian Istria also uses the name Teran for a related but distinct grape; a 2017 EU derogation allowing Croatian producers to put Teran on labels alongside 'Hrvatska Istra' was contested by Slovenia in the EU courts.
si-teran.terroir: Terra rossa over limestone on the Karst plateau.
si-teran.nerd_note: Teran's maximum yield (90 hl/ha) is higher than other Slovenian PDOs because Refošk on the Karst crops modestly anyway; its high natural acidity is the defining analytical trait.

si-vipavska-dolina.name: Vipavska dolina
si-vipavska-dolina.grapes: Zelen, Pinela, Rebula, Malvazija, Laški rizling, Sauvignon, Chardonnay; Merlot, Barbera, Refošk
si-vipavska-dolina.summary: The Vipava valley runs west from the Nanos plateau towards Gorizia, a corridor where the bora wind blows hard enough to tip lorries; growers build stone walls and plant trees as windbreaks. About 2,100 ha on flysch slopes make fresh and macerated whites from Rebula, Malvazija, Laški rizling, Sauvignon and the two natives, Zelen (herbal, gooseberry-like) and Pinela (light and nervy), plus reds from Merlot, Barbera and Refošk. Batič, Mlečnik, Guerila, Burja, Sutor, Tilia and Lepa Vida are among the leading estates.
si-vipavska-dolina.terroir: Flysch and marl on the valley sides, alluvium on the floor; sub-Mediterranean climate swept by the bora, which keeps vines dry and healthy.
si-vipavska-dolina.nerd_note: Zelen and Pinela were nearly extinct in the 1980s; Vipava growers rebuilt them from a few old vineyards, and both are now protected local specialities.

sites.name: Stara trta (Old Vine), Maribor
sites.text: Trained along the south facade of a house in Maribor's Lent quarter, this Žametovka vine is more than 400 years old and listed by Guinness as the oldest vine in the world. It still gives 35 to 55 kg of grapes a year, enough for 15 to 35 litres of wine. Cuttings grow at 130 official sites in Slovenia and 84 abroad.

sites.name: Ptujska klet, Ptuj
sites.text: Ptuj's winery claims a symbolic beginning in 1239, when the Minorites built a monastery with a wine cellar in the town centre. Its archive holds Zlata trta 1917, the oldest Slovenian archive wine, hidden from the occupiers in World War II by Pavel Ornig.

sites.name: Vinag cellar, Maribor
sites.text: Under Maribor's Trg svobode lies a vast cellar network on several levels, among the largest in Central Europe. It was the core of Vinag, the city's big socialist-era wine company, and is now used for tours, tastings and ageing.

sites.name: Jeruzalem
sites.text: A hilltop hamlet in the Ljutomer-Ormož hills, Jeruzalem is said to have been named by crusaders who saw it as a promised land. Its steep, terraced amphitheatres of Šipon, Laški rizling, Sauvignon and Traminec are among the most photographed vineyards in Slovenia.

sites.name: Haloze hills
sites.text: The Haloze hills south of Ptuj, along the Croatian border, are among the steepest vineyard landscapes in Central Europe. Small terraced plots on marl give racy Laški rizling, Šipon and Sauvignon.

sites.name: Radgonske gorice, Gornja Radgona
sites.text: Gornja Radgona's winery traces its sparkling-wine tradition to 1852, when Clotar Bouvier began making traditional-method wine here. Its Zlata Radgonska penina is Slovenia's best-known sparkling brand, aged in cellars cut into the hill.

sites.name: Lendavske gorice
sites.text: The vineyard hill above Lendava in Prekmurje looks out over the Pannonian plain to Hungary and Croatia, with a wooden lookout tower and traditional press houses among Laški rizling and Šipon vines.

sites.name: Movia
sites.text: The Kristančič family's estate in Ceglo has made wine since 1820, with vineyards on both sides of the Italian border. Aleš Kristančič made it famous for long-macerated Lunar Rebula and Puro, a sparkling wine sold undisgorged.

sites.name: Klinec
sites.text: Aleks Klinec's estate and guesthouse in Medana farms biodynamically and makes long-macerated whites (Rebula, Malvazija, Jakot) aged in acacia, mulberry and cherry wood, a reference for Brda orange wine.

sites.name: Kabaj
sites.text: Frenchman Jean-Michel Morel married into the Kabaj family at Šlovrenc in Brda; their macerated Rebula and Amfora wines, fermented in Georgian qvevri, helped build Slovenian orange wine's international profile.

sites.name: Edi Simčič
sites.text: This Vipolže estate on the Italian border is one of Brda's leading names. Its single-vineyard Kozana Chardonnay and Duet Lex Merlot-based reds show the district's capacity for structured, ageable wines.

sites.name: Dobrovo Castle and Klet Brda
sites.text: Dobrovo's Renaissance castle anchors Goriška Brda's capital village. Klet Brda, the cooperative founded here in 1957, gathers around 400 growers and is Slovenia's largest wine producer.

sites.name: Batič
sites.text: The Batič family's biodynamic estate at Šempas in the Vipava valley makes macerated whites, the Zaria blend and Angel, a sweet white. It was among the Vipava pioneers of skin contact and natural winemaking.

sites.name: Tomaj and Dutovlje, the Teran villages
sites.text: Tomaj and neighbouring Dutovlje sit at the heart of Teran country on the Kras, among red-earth vineyards walled in limestone. Family osmice (seasonal farm taverns) pour Teran with pršut.

sites.name: Bizeljsko repnice
sites.text: Bizeljsko's repnice are caves dug by hand into quartz sand beneath the vineyards, first for storing turnips and later wine and sparkling wine, which keep at a steady temperature. Several, such as Najger's, are open for tastings.

sites.name: Trška gora
sites.text: Trška gora, a hill above Novo mesto crowned by a pilgrimage church, is covered with small vineyards and zidanice cottages: the classic Cviček landscape of Dolenjska.

sites.name: Metlika
sites.text: Metlika on the Kolpa is the wine capital of Bela krajina and home of Metliška črnina. Its castle houses the Slovenian Fire-Fighting Museum and a regional museum with viticulture exhibits, and the town's wine fair each spring showcases the district.
